notes: §1985:XI.4.3.3 SR3: "A RETURN statement may only be used within the range of an output procedure associated with a SORT or MERGE statement for file-name-1." WalkProgram calls GateReleaseReturnRange below 2002, which seeds ProcedureReach.Closure (followGoTo) with the output procedures of the SORT and MERGE statements naming the file and reports COBOL7081 for a RETURN outside; since kb/Work PB5572 landed it asks a declarative RETURN too, refused where no output procedure for the file exists. Re-read 2026-11-15 (registrar landing records-1985-reread): the adjudicator's and refuter's probes of op-20261115/open-rows-1985 re-run on this branch's build (main 2722570af0) at --std 85, logs op-20261115/registrar-1985-reread/log-fmt.txt, log-misc.txt, log-witnesses.txt. Holds: RETURN in the output procedure and reached from it by GO TO, an ALTERed GO TO, GO TO DEPENDING, THRU, PERFORM, RETURN INTO / NOT AT END in a PERFORM UNTIL, and in a contained program's own SORT runs (refute-b t1-t5, t9, t12; work-b RL1 AAA ZZZ); RETURN in the main line after the SORT, in the input procedure and of another SD in this SD's output procedure is refused COBOL7081 (work-b RT2, RT3, refute-b t6). The CALL half of §1985:XI.4.4.4 GR10 is not expressible at 85: RETURN names file-name-1 and the SD format prints no GLOBAL clause, and both attempts are refused (RT4 COBOL1639, RT5 COBOL1970); kb/Work PB5628's RETURN half has nothing to fix at 85. kb/Work PB5768 (wave 20262068): the declarative RETURN was exempted wholesale once any procedure existed, although GR7/GR10 admit only declaratives executed as a result of the range's statements; VersionConformancePass.DeclarativeExecutableFromRange now exempts a USE AFTER STANDARD ERROR procedure's statement only when the range holds an input-output statement on a file the USE names (any file for an open-mode USE) or a CALL, so refute-b/t13 (a range with neither) is refused COBOL7081 (witness pb5768-return-in-declarative-not-executable-from-range-85) and pb5572_release_in_declarative_of_input_procedure_85 still runs.

next.reason: 1985: "A RETURN statement may only be used within the range of an output procedure associated with a SORT or MERGE statement"; 2023: "may be executed only when it is within the range of an output procedure ... If it is executed at any other time, the EC-FLOW-RETURN". 1985 limits where RETURN may be used as a syntax rule. 2023 states only an execution-time rule: RETURN executed outside an output procedure sets EC-FLOW-RETURN.
